speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have experienced an episode of loss of consciousness; to help you, please describe exactly what happened, including any warning symptoms, how long you were out, and if you lost any memory of the event. Also, do you have any history of heart disease, diabetes, or seizures?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Situational Syncope (Micturition Syncope).

The clinical presentation of loss of consciousness immediately after urination, with rapid recovery and no confusion, is classic for this reflex-mediated event. Given the patient is 53, I need to assess for underlying cardiovascular risk factors.

REQUEST TEST: ECG (Electrocardiogram)
